messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a regression in prefix cache hit-rate and a correlated memory spike after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak (deploy abc123). Hit-rate for hot prefixes on xg-rt (GPU pool) dropped from ~78% to ~42% during the 10:00–10:30 window. p95 latency jumped ~35ms for small prompts. logs/snippet attached below.

aj: ugh. any obvious change in key normalization or batching?

maria: The change was to prefer the 'fast-attn' kernel for sequences <=256 and to enable micro-batching heuristics that split long multisentence prompts into smaller segments to reduce tail latency. Hypothesis: the segmentation + kernel path alters how prompt IDs are canonicalized and creates more unique KV keys, reducing reuse. Also saw a small uptick in slab fragmentation on GPU-side cache.

leo: can you paste the hit-rate delta per-model?

maria: quick dump: 
```
model | pre-change hit% | post-change hit%
redwood-xl-8k | 79.1 | 44.3
redwood-m-3b  | 74.5 | 41.8
redwood-compact-1.2 | 82.0 | 48.0
```
Also sampler traces show a 3x increase in unique prefix keys for incoming workload.

sasha: did eviction behavior change? TTLs?

maria: TTL config unchanged. Eviction throughput spiked — eviction loop running more frequently because active set cardinality grew. Memory pressure on GPU reached 86% vs normal ~62% (short lived). OOMs avoided but there were a few short-lived kernel fallback events logged by ops-bot.

ops-bot: [alert] kernel-fallbacks=24; evict-loop-runs=1123; gpu-mem-peak=86%; fallbacks->cpu=7

devon: probable root cause: key-shaping. The micro-batching introduces different boundary tokens or different tokenization splits which we then use raw as cache keys. If the keying function is suffix-sensitive we get explosion. do we use canonical prompt-normalization everywhere?

maria: not everywhere. runtime/path A uses normalized prompt.strip() + collapse-whitespace, path B (fast-attn) currently uses raw token span + start-offset for key.

aj: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: force fast-attn to use canonical keying (cheap flag) and measure hit-rate; 2) tune prefill affinity to avoid splitting hot prefixes across micro-batches; 3) increase GPU slab reservation temporarily to reduce eviction churn.

leo: agree. Also add a lightweight sampling profiler to log canonicalization mismatch rate per-request (bool key_normalized). we need a number for cost benefit.

maria: ran cheap experiment on staging: forcing canonical keying for fast-attn restored hit-rate to ~75% and reduced eviction runs by ~60%. p95 latency returned near baseline. however we observed a small CPU encoding overhead (~1.8ms median). tradeoff seems fine.

sasha: great. what's the rollout plan? can we hotfix?

aj: we can flip a runtime flag for the fast-attn path, no binary change. I'll push flag -> canary to 5% of traffic in gpu-us-west first. need ops runbook for memory bump and rollback.

devon: follow-up: we should also inspect prefill/compact affinity heuristics. The micro-batching tends to break contiguous prefixes used for caching. Proposal: coalesce contiguous prompts when they share the same prompt hash before issuing micro-batches. That would reduce cache key fragmentation. Might be slightly more complex.

maria: added a quick checklist: 
- (P0) aj: push runtime flag to force canonical keying for fast-attn (canary 5%) — start 2812348100 
- (P0) ops: temporarily bump GPU slab reserve by +10% on canary hosts — start 2812348200 
- (P1) devon: prototype pre-batch coalescer to keep hot prefixes contiguous (PR review by end of week) 
- (P2) leo: add key_normalized telemetry and per-model unique-prefix-count metric (ops retention 7d) 

aj: I'll do the flag and metric gating. tagging @ops for the slab bump.

sasha: ops: are there limitations to slab bump? side-effects?

ops-bot: ops-note: slab bump must be staggered across hosts to avoid reduced overall capacity. Recommend 10% on 10% of hosts initially, monitor eviction-rate & latency.

devon: long-term fixes: 
- unify key canonicalization code paths (runtime + fast-attn + fallback)
- add deterministic tokenization boundaries for micro-batching so keys don't vary by split heuristic
- consider prefix-key fingerprinting (hash canonicalized prompt + model + pinned-metadata) to reduce key length variance

maria: agreement: unify canonicalization first, then address batching coalescer. I'm adding an entry to the OOM playbook about this regression pattern (kernel-routing + split heuristics => key explosion).

leo: one more ask: can we run a simulation on historical traffic with the micro-batch splitting applied to see expected unique-key growth before enabling micro-batch heuristics broadly? that would've caught this.

maria: yes i've queued a simulation job. estimate 3h run. will post results here when done.

aj: plan to monitor: prefix_hitrate, eviction_runs, gpu_mem_percent, fallback_count, p95_latency. dash: /dash/eng/runtime/prefix-regressions (w/ alerts at +/-15% hit delta).

sasha: ack. thanks team. update in-thread once canary started. :thumbsup:

maria: canary rolled out at 2812348100, initial numbers look good: hit% on canary 73.8, eviction_runs -58%, cpu-encoding +1.7ms. leaving canary for 30m then widen.

leo: nice. if stable, proceed to 50% over next 2 hours.

devon: logging note: when you widen, please add sampling for the token boundaries before and after coalescer so we can measure fragmentation delta.

maria: will do. closing loop once we have full rollout. thanks everyone.
